'''William Browder''' (January 6, 1934 – February 4, 2025) was an American mathematician, who specialized in [[algebraic topology]], [[differential topology]] and [[differential geometry]]. He served as president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 1989 to 1991.

==Early life and education==
William Browder was born in a Jewish hospital in [[Harlem]], [[New York City]] on January 6, 1934,<ref name="pit"/><ref name="cv">[https://www.math.princeton.edu/WebCV/BrowderCV.pdf Curriculum vitae] from Browder's web site, retrieved October 6, 2010.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=William Browder {{!}} Office of the Dean of the Faculty |url=https://dof.princeton.edu/people/william-browder |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=dof.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> the son of Raisa (née Berkman), a [[Russia]]n [[Jew]]ish woman from [[Saint Petersburg]], and [[Communist Party USA|American Communist Party]] leader [[Earl Browder]], from [[Wichita, Kansas]]. His father had moved to the [[Soviet Union]] in 1927, where he met and married Raisa. Their first two sons, [[Felix Browder|Felix]] and [[Andrew Browder|Andrew]], were born in Moscow in 1931.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Browder_William.html|title=Browder_William biography|website=www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk|access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> William attended local public schools in Yonkers for early schooling and graduated from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] with a [[B.S.]] degree in 1954. He was a instructor at the University of Rochester from 1957 to 1958 and at Cornell University from 1958 until 1963. In August 1957, his original thesis fell apart when his advisor, [[John Coleman Moore]], found a problem with the idea. However, William came up with a new idea which was titled ''[[Homology (mathematics)|Homology]] of [[Loop Space]]s.'' He received his [[Ph.D.]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1958.<ref name="cv"/><ref>Students of John Coleman Moore, MathGenealogy, [https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=4350]</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
From 1964 onwards, Browder was a professor at [[Princeton University]]; he was chair of the mathematics department at Princeton from 1971 to 1973. He was editor of the journal ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' from 1969 to 1981, and president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 1989 to 1991.<ref name="cv"/>

Browder was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1980, the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1984, and the [[Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters]] in 1990.<ref name="cv"/> In 1994, a conference was held at Princeton in celebration of his 60th birthday.<ref name="pit">{{citation|title=Prospects in topology: proceedings of a conference in honor of William Browder|volume=138|series=Annals of mathematics studies|editor-first=Frank|editor-last=Quinn|publisher=[[Princeton University Press]]|year=1995|isbn=978-0-691-02728-9}}.</ref> A conference was held at Princeton on the occasion of his retirement in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Panorama of Topology: A Conference in Honor of William Browder |url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/conference/browder2012/index.html |website=math.princeton.edu |publisher=Princeton University Department of Mathematics |access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> Browder advised 30 Ph.D. students in his career as well as multiple undergraduate students.<ref name=":0" />

== Death ==
Browder died on February 4, 2025, at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite web |title=William Browder January 6,1934–February 4, 2025 |url=https://www.matherhodge.com/obituaries/William-Browder?obId=39486272 |access-date=February 20, 2025 |website=William Browder Obituary}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=In Memoriam: William Browder *58 &#124; Princeton Alumni Weekly | url=https://paw.princeton.edu/article/memoriam-william-browder-58 }}</ref>
